newsitem.title: USA: Tropical storm warnings issued in Caribbean.
newsitem.headline: Tropical storm warnings issued in Caribbean.

text.p: Tropical storm warnings were issued from Martinique through the U.S. Virgin Islands on Saturday as Tropical Storm Hortense approached the eastern Caribbean, the National Hurricane Center said.
A tropical storm watch, indicating that storm conditions could arrive within 36 hours, was issued for Puerto Rico. Storm warnings are posted by forecasters 24 hours ahead of possible landfall.
The hurricane center said a hurricane watch or warning could be issued for part of the area by Saturday night.
At 2 p.m. EDT (1900 GMT), Hortense was located about 50 miles (85 km) east of Guadeloupe and Dominica, at latitude 15.9 north and longitude 60.5 west.

The storm carried maximum sustained winds of about 60 mph (95 kmh) and was moving west-northwest at 11 mph (18 kmh), a track that forecasters said was expected to continue for the next 24 hours. Further strengthening also was possible.
Hortense would become a hurricane if sustained winds reached 74 mph (119 kmh).
"On this track the storm will be passing through the Leeward and northern Windward Islands today and Sunday," said Ed Rappaport of the National Hurricane Center.
Hortense gathered strength in the wake of Hurricane Fran, which hit the U.S. coast on Thursday, wreaking havoc through the Carolinas and leaving at least 21 people dead.
Hortense was upgraded to tropical storm status at mid-morning on Saturday.

The string of tiny Leeward Islands -- including Martinique, Dominica, Guadeloupe, Antigua, Montserrat, the U.S. Virgin Islands and the British Virgin Islands -- immediately issued tropical storm warnings and urged residents to prepare.
Forecasters said it was too early to predict whether Hortense would threaten the U.S. mainland.
"It's way too early to know if the continental United States is going to be affected. There's so much time that any number of factors could turn it away," Rappaport said.
In three days, Hortense was expected to be near Haiti and the Dominican Republic, which share the island of Hispaniola. The island is about 700 miles (1,126 km) south of Florida.
Tropical storm force winds extended outward up to 60 miles (95 km) east of the center.
Hortense was also dumping rain of up to 10 inches (25 cms) along its path. Forecasters warned that even more rain could fall as Hortense moved over mountains, increasing the risk of flash floods.
